observations:
Torah #118 is an extremely compact teaching (7 lines) with one single, tightly unified bechina cluster. All bechina-connected nodes belong to Package 1 (צַדִּיק הַדּוֹר, מֹשֶׁה, וּמָשִׁיחַ). There is no second independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts in this Torah.

The two gap concepts identified (רוּחַ פִּיו and רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא) both attach naturally to Package 1 as satellite bechina-equivalents of the ruach d'Mashiach dimension. They do not form an independent thematic family warranting a new package.

The good/evil mirror structure: Torah #118 has no explicit evil mirror package. The Torah is almost entirely a positive teaching about the tzaddik's spiritual identity and the cosmic significance of Torah novelties. The concept of חֹל (profanation/lowering) that appears in the eitza section is not a full evil cluster — it is a structural consequence of Israel's transgressions (פְּשָׁעֵינוּ), mentioned briefly as the mechanism of the tzaddik's suffering. There are no evil-domain bechina nodes in Torah #118.

The Torah's single-argument structure:
  [Stage 1 — Identity equation] Every tzaddik = Moshe = Mashiach [Package 1: good]
  [Stage 2 — The ruach dimension] Chidushei Torah = Mashiach (his spirit hovers there) [Package 1: good]
  [Stage 3 — Consequence / eitza] Therefore the tzaddik suffers (Mashiach suffers for Israel) → and this is why translating Torah to the vernacular is necessary [eitza edge, outside packages]
  [Stage 4 — Condition] All this applies only because of our sins; elevated individuals grasp Torah as it was said [contextual framing]

Conclusion: Torah #118 contains exactly one package, no evil mirror, and no secondary good package. This is consistent with the brevity and concentrated focus of the teaching.
